increments.title: Templates: navigation, Manage templates and creating a template through the journey
increments.detail: DR2.1 adds templates so a trader can start repeat consignments without re-entering them. Templates are stored by the animals backend as records apart from notifications, owned by the signed-in organisation; the template pages and template-mode journey are in the animals frontend; both frontends' navigation gains Templates.
acceptanceCriteria: In both the animals frontend and the INS frontend a signed-in trader's navigation offers, in order, Dashboard, Templates, Address book, Manage account and Log out; Templates is active on every template page and Address book on every address-book page. (prototype:dr2-1-source p1-021, p1-023; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p1-011, p15-015; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-011; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 p1-010)

A 'Manage templates' page (heading and title 'Manage templates', description 'Select, manage or create new notification templates', a 'Create new template' button) lists the organisation's templates under 'My templates' with a 'Show 1-N of N results' count and a 'Sort by:' select. (prototype:dr2-1-source p14-001, p14-002, p14-003, p14-006, p14-007; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p15-002, p15-003; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-002, p6-003)

Each template card is labelled 'Template <title>', shows its category and title with 'View template' and 'Use template' links, and lists Commodity, Origin, Consignee and Consignor. (prototype:dr2-1-source p14-008, p14-014, p14-015, p14-016; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-004, p6-005)
A trader never sees another organisation's templates. (ruling:sam-2026-10-07 p1-010)
'Create new template' asks 'Enter template name' (caption 'Create a new template'); a blank name saves as 'Untitled template'. (prototype:dr2-1-source p14-023, p14-024, p14-027)

The journey then runs from the origin page in template mode: the overview shows a 'Template' tag and the template name, is headed 'Template tasklist', has no Documents section, and ends with 'Review template' and 'Return to manage templates'. (prototype:dr2-1-source p14-029, p12-007, p12-017, p12-033, p12-040, p12-043; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p15-057, p15-061)
In template mode the arrival date, documents and declaration are not asked. (prototype:dr2-1-source p6-022, p10-003, p1-063)

A saved template keeps the origin, commodity and species, numbers, identifiers, reason and purpose, certified for, unweaned answer, port of entry, transport, transporter, place of origin, CPH and contact address, and never an arrival date or documents. (prototype:dr2-1-source p14-041, p14-042, p14-043, p14-044, p14-045)

openQuestions: c-020: Where a real service has a feature DR2.1 does not show at all, is it removed? Default followed: DR2.1's one-page list and live search replace server pagination and the in-place details; the server search stays as the route without JavaScript.
increments.notes: Combines the picker layout, role filtering and the no-choice save: all on the picker page. Depends on inc-022 for address uses.

increments.title: Adding an address from a picker uses DR2.1's journey add-address page and selects it
increments.detail: DR2.1 adds and selects a missing address without leaving the journey. The address book has one writer, so the INS frontend's add page, reached through the existing journey handshake, shows DR2.1's journey add-address content and returns to the animals journey with the address selected or not as the trader chose.
acceptanceCriteria: A picker's 'Add a new address' opens a page captioned 'Add new address' and headed 'Add address and contact details'. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-077, p8-079; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-022)
Origin-side parties enter an address in any country by hand; destination-side parties search UK addresses or enter one by hand. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-081, p8-082)
'What else should this address be used for?' (hint 'This address is being added as a <role> address...') offers the other roles on the same side. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-092, p8-094, p8-095)

'Save and select' saves the address to the address book with the role and the ticked uses, selects it and returns to the consignment addresses page with '<name> address added to your address book'. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-110, p8-009; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-027; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-080)
'Save and return to address page' saves it and returns to the picker, where it is listed and not yet selected. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-111)
openQuestions: c-011: Does DR2.1's journey add-address page live in the animals frontend, or in the INS frontend's add page reached through the existing handshake? Default followed: in the INS frontend, through the existing journey handshake; the animals frontend stays read-only.
c-010: What real address source answers 'Search for an address'? Default followed: the INS backend's address lookup made production-ready (inc-025).
c-012: Does every address form ask for 'County (optional)'? Default followed: yes, the journey add-address page included.
increments.notes: One slice across both frontends: the INS add page in journey mode and the animals journey's return. Depends on inc-029 for the picker and on inc-025 for the UK search.

increments.title: The contact address is chosen from the organisation's branch addresses
increments.detail: DR2.1 and DR1 limit the contact to the trader's own branch addresses and explain who the contact is.
acceptanceCriteria: The contact address page is headed 'Contact address for consignment' with no caption and opens with 'This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-116, p8-117, p8-118)

It then shows 'Select an address' and 'If the correct address is not shown, add a new branch address, then return to this page.', linking to adding an address in the address book. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-119, p8-121)

It lists only the organisation's branch addresses, as radios with the name as label and the address as hint. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-122, p8-123; document:dr1-parity-backlog p7-024; document:dr1-parity-notes p1-020)
Continuing with no address chosen shows 'Select a contact address'. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-126)
A branch address added from this page is selected on return. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-126; document:dr1-parity-backlog p7-006)
increments.notes: One page. Depends on inc-022 for branch uses and inc-024 for adding a branch address.

increments.title: The permanent address becomes a consignment party, answered for every animal at once
increments.detail: DR2.1 asks the permanent address of cats, dogs and ferrets as a consignment party on its own page instead of inside each identification record. Today's commodity list offers cats and dogs; ferrets join when master data supplies them (inc-010).
acceptanceCriteria: When cats or dogs are in the consignment, the consignment addresses page has a 'Permanent address' section (hint 'A permanent address is where an animal:' with two bullets, link 'Add a permanent address'), which reads 'Permanent addresses added for N animals' once answered. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-030, p9-023, p9-073)

The 'Permanent address' page (caption 'Consignment parties', the fraud warning, the definition, 'Where will their permanent address be?') has one card per animal headed '<species> <n>' showing its identifiers. (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-024, p9-033, p9-034, p9-036)

Each card offers 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' (hinted with the destination address) and 'Enter a new address' (hint 'This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination.'), which reveals name, address, town, county, postcode, email and phone with no country. (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-037, p9-038, p9-039, p9-041, p9-042)
Summary errors add 'for <animal>', and choosing the destination before one is added shows 'Add a place of destination before you can continue'. (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-043, p9-052, p9-053, p9-054)
The identification page no longer collects a permanent address, and its saved-animals table has no 'Permanent address' column. (prototype:dr2-1-source p5-060; document:dr1-parity-backlog p6-058)
A notification's permanent addresses are still saved and shown on the review. (repo:frontend p6-105)

sources.ref: views/design-release-2.1 permanent address section and page
permanent address rows, now built (conflict c-022)

openQuestions: c-012: Does every address form ask for 'County (optional)'? Default followed: yes, the permanent address included.
increments.notes: Combines adding the permanent address page with taking it off the identification page: one move, so the address is never asked twice or lost. Depends on inc-027 (the section layout). Which commodities need a permanent address already follows DR2.1 for today's list (req-081, met), so it no longer waits for inc-004, which is dropped. Under the c-023 default no environment offers ferrets yet, so acceptance names cats and dogs; ferrets take the same section once inc-010 lands (req-116).

increments.title: The transporter type and add pages follow DR2.1 and check required fields
increments.detail: DR2.1 words the transporter type and add pages differently, requires a type, checks every required field even on a blank form, and offers an address search over Northern Ireland addresses for commercial transporters.
acceptanceCriteria: The transporter type page warns 'Check the transporter list before adding new transporters to avoid duplicates.', has the visually hidden legend 'Choose a transporter type', offers 'Private transporter' and 'Commercial' (hint 'This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland.') and refuses no choice with 'Select a transporter type'. (prototype:dr2-1-source p7-049, p7-050, p7-053, p7-054, p7-055, p7-057)

The private transporter page is headed 'Add a private transporter' with no intro sentence, and its country select starts on United Kingdom with no blank option. (prototype:dr2-1-source p7-062, p7-066, p7-072)
The commercial transporter page is headed 'Add a commercial transporter' and asks 'Postcode or Zip code'. (prototype:dr2-1-source p7-086, p7-091)

Saving either add page, even left blank, checks every required field; the commercial page's errors read 'Enter a transporter authorisation number' and 'Enter a postcode or Zip code'. (prototype:dr2-1-source p7-075, p7-076, p7-096, p7-103)
The commercial page offers 'Search for an address' with 'Enter address manually', which is always offered and adds the transporter without a search result. (prototype:dr2-1-source p7-093)

On the local workspace stack, a commercial transporter search offers no address outside Northern Ireland: a search the address lookup answers with its England addresses lists none of them. (prototype:dr2-1-source p7-093; repo:insfrontend p5-074)

In CDP environments, a commercial transporter search lists Northern Ireland addresses from the address lookup and no address outside Northern Ireland. (prototype:dr2-1-source p7-093; repo:insfrontend p5-067)

features/transport transporter-add, private and commercial details

openQuestions: c-010: What real address source answers the commercial transporter page's 'Search for an address', and should trade-imports-stub gain Northern Ireland addresses? Default followed: the INS backend's address lookup answers it; on the local workspace stack it answers from trade-imports-stub unchanged, so the search returns no address and only the exclusion of addresses outside Northern Ireland and manual entry are shown there; in CDP environments it returns Northern Ireland addresses only. trade-imports-stub is not changed by this programme.
c-020: Where a real service has a feature DR2.1 does not show at all, is it removed? Default followed: kept unless DR2.1 shows another way to do the same job.
c-012: Does every address form ask for 'County (optional)'? Default followed: yes, the transporter forms included.
increments.notes: Combines the type page and both add pages: one add-a-transporter flow. Depends on inc-023 (transporters saved to the address book) and inc-025 (the address lookup). Acceptance for the search is written per environment, as the c-010 default settles it: the workspace stack's address-lookup simulator in trade-imports-stub holds only England addresses and is not changed by this programme, so locally the test proves only that none is offered and that manual entry works; a Northern Ireland result is observed in CDP environments.

increments.title: The journey's transporter list searches as the trader types, links each transporter and confirms an addition
increments.detail: DR2.1's transporter list filters as the trader types, places 'Add a transporter' above the table, links each row to the transporter's page in the address book, and confirms a newly added transporter.
acceptanceCriteria: The 'Transporter details' search ('Search', hint 'Name, address or approval number') filters the rows as the trader types, and the server search still works without JavaScript. (prototype:dr2-1-source p7-015, p7-016, p7-017)
The secondary 'Add a transporter' button sits above the table. (prototype:dr2-1-source p7-020)
Each row has a 'View details' link to that transporter's page in the address book, with a way back to the list. (prototype:dr2-1-source p7-021, p7-026; document:dr1-parity-backlog p8-016)

After a transporter is added from the journey, the list shows a one-time 'Success' banner '<Name> transporter added' (first letter capital, the rest lower case), or 'Transporter added' when it has no name. (prototype:dr2-1-source p7-045, p7-046, p7-047)

sources.ref: transporter record page left out until the address book settled

openQuestions: c-020: Where a real service has a feature DR2.1 does not show at all, is it removed? Default followed: the server search stays as the route without JavaScript.
increments.notes: Combines the list's search, layout and links with its success banner: one page. Depends on inc-023 for transporters' pages in the address book.

increments.title: The dashboard shows the organisation's own notifications as DR2.1 cards
increments.detail: DR2.1 identifies a consignment by what, from where, when and between whom, and shows a trader only their own work. The INS read model takes the consignee and consignor names, number of animals, commodity common name, arrival date, status and organisation from the animals backend's events, and the dashboard's table becomes cards.
acceptanceCriteria: Every dashboard list, tab, count and search shows only the signed-in organisation's notifications; a notification another organisation made never appears. (repo:insbackend p1-068, p1-069; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 p1-010)
Each notification shows as a card labelled for screen readers 'Notification <reference>', with the reference as its heading. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-046; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p1-065)

A card's first row shows Commodity, Arrival date (dd/mm/yyyy), Consignee and Notification status, and its second row Number of animals, Origin and Consignor. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-053, p13-054, p13-055)
A submitted notification's status reads 'Submitted' as plain text and a draft shows a 'Draft' tag. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-061, p13-062)
A change saved in the journey, such as a new consignee, shows on the notification's card. (prototype:dr2-1-source p12-097; repo:insbackend p1-002)
openQuestions: c-007: Is organisation scoping of the dashboard lists, counts and searches built in this programme, though ins-backend deferred it to a later ticket? Default followed: yes; the INS read model records each notification's organisation from its events and the INS frontend sends the session's organisation.
c-013: Is the arrival date the arrival at the port of entry or at the place of destination? Default followed: the port of entry, labelled 'Arrival date' on the dashboard card.
c-006: What is built for states no real service records? Default followed: action required comes from the animals backend (inc-014); the card shows it from inc-039.
increments.notes: Combines organisation scoping, the read-model fields and the cards: the fields cannot be observed without the cards, and the cards must never show another organisation's work. Built on today's INS dashboard page; inc-040 moves it into DR2.1's home and Live animals pages.
increments.gate: Check organisation scoping and the read-model fields: every later dashboard row filters, counts and searches them.

increments.title: The notification list has DR2.1's tabs, search, sort and pages of eight
increments.detail: DR2.1 separates work in flight from drafts and finished notifications, lets a trader find a notification by what they remember about it, sorts the list, and pages it in eights. The list is always sorted, as DR1 ruled.
acceptanceCriteria: The list has one search field labelled 'Search by' with the hint 'Keyword, notification number, commodity, consignee or consignor' and a magnifying-glass Search button. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-026, p13-027)
A search matches any part of a notification's reference, commodity, consignee or consignor, and the searched text stays in the field. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-027; repo:insbackend p1-059)

A 'Sort by:' select offers 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date' and orders the list; the list is always sorted, Newest first by default, with no 'Select one' option. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-043; document:dr1-parity-notes p1-012)

Three tabs read 'In progress (N)', 'Draft' and 'Completed', each with a subheading ('Notifications in progress', 'Draft notifications', 'Completed notifications'); In progress lists submitted and action-required notifications, Draft lists drafts and Completed lists completed ones. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-037, p13-038, p13-039, p13-040; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p1-061, p1-062, p1-063; prototype:dr2-1-specs p5-042, p5-043)
Lists show 8 notifications a page with numbered pagination and Previous and Next links, and page links keep the tab and the sort. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-041, p13-042, p13-043)

sources.ref: list search, sort and page size

openQuestions: c-002: Do DR1's rulings inc-030 and inc-031, made on the animals-frontend dashboard, apply to the DR2.1 dashboard in the INS frontend? Default followed: yes; every list is always sorted, Newest first by default, with no 'Select one' option.
c-006: What is built for states no real service records? Default followed: the Completed tab is built and stays empty until a service records completion.
increments.notes: Combines search, sort, tabs and paging: they share one list query and one set of page links.

increments.title: The notification list can be narrowed by arrival and status
increments.detail: DR2.1 lets a trader narrow the list by arrival date and status; a real service applies the filters the prototype only displays.
acceptanceCriteria: The list has a collapsible 'Additional filters' section, open when any filter is set. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-030)
'By arrival date' radios (Today, Tomorrow, Next 7 days) narrow the list to notifications arriving then. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-031)
'By date range' start and end dates, each hinted 'For example, 27/3/2026', narrow the list to notifications arriving in that range. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-032)
A 'Status' select (Select one, Action required, Submitted, Completed) narrows the list to that status. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-035, p13-036; repo:insbackend p1-044)
openQuestions: c-006: What is built for states no real service records? Default followed: Action required comes from the animals backend; Completed stays empty until a service records completion.
increments.notes: Kept apart from inc-036 so each stays reviewable. The INS frontend's client scripts belong to the live-animals-journey theme, so the date range must work as plain date fields.

increments.title: Dashboard cards offer actions by status
increments.detail: DR1 rejected flattening the card to Copy as new and View; that judgement carries to the INS dashboard's cards.
acceptanceCriteria: A draft's card offers Resume, Copy as new and Delete. (document:dr1-parity-notes p1-011; document:dr1-parity-backlog p3-041)

A submitted notification's card offers View, Amend, Copy as new and Delete; Amend leads to the notification's 'Amend this notification' confirmation. (document:dr1-parity-backlog p3-042; prototype:dr2-1-source p13-048)
A card for a notification being amended offers Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment and Delete. (document:dr1-parity-backlog p3-044; prototype:dr2-1-source p13-049)

Each action does what the same action does in the journey: Resume opens the overview, View the notification's page, Copy as new a new draft, Cancel amendment the cancel-amendment confirmation and Delete the delete page. (repo:frontend p3-047, p3-050, p3-052)
openQuestions: c-002: Do DR1's rulings inc-030 and inc-031 apply to the DR2.1 dashboard in the INS frontend? Default followed: yes; cards keep status-driven actions.
increments.notes: Depends on inc-012 for the notification page's amend confirmation that Amend leads to. The read model must tell a draft, a submitted notification and one being amended apart.

increments.title: Notifications needing action are flagged on their cards and gathered on an Action needed page
increments.detail: DR2.1 flags submitted notifications that still owe something before import and gathers them on a 'View tasks' drill-down.
acceptanceCriteria: A notification needing action shows on its card in the error style with a red marker, an 'Action required' tag and its message: 'ITAHC is missing' when no ITAHC document is attached, otherwise 'Information is missing' when required animal identifiers are incomplete. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-052, p13-063, p13-064, p11-148, p11-149; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p1-071)

An 'Action needed' page (caption 'Action needed', heading 'Tasks requiring your attention', description 'Add missing information or upload documents to prevent your consignment from being delayed.') lists the notifications needing action for its category. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-079, p13-080, p13-081, p13-082; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p1-088, p1-089; prototype:dr2-1-specs p5-065)

It has the same search and sort as the list, a 'Show <first>-<last> of <total> results' count, 8 a page, and a Back link to the category list. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-083, p13-085, p13-086; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p1-094; prototype:dr2-1-specs p5-066)

sources.ref: views/design-release-2.1 dashboard card action-required state and action needed page

openQuestions: c-006: What is built for states no real service records? Default followed: Action required is built from the items outstanding at submission, recorded by the animals backend (inc-014) and carried to the INS read model.
increments.notes: Combines the card flag with the page that gathers flagged notifications: one state, two views. Depends on inc-014 for action required and inc-036 for the shared search and sort.

increments.title: The dashboard home and the Live animals page follow DR2.1
increments.detail: DR2.1 makes the dashboard a signed-in landing page that sends the trader to what needs attention, with a page per notification category. Only live animals is built; states no real service records are built empty or not at all.
acceptanceCriteria: The Dashboard navigation item of both frontends opens the dashboard home, and the Address book item of both opens the INS address book. (document:dr1-parity-notes p1-014; prototype:dr2-1-source p1-083)

The home has the caption 'Dashboard' above the heading 'Import notification service', a primary 'Create new' button and a secondary 'Use template' button to Manage templates. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-001, p13-004, p13-006, p13-007; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p1-028; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-012)
'Create new' starts a live-animals notification straight on its origin page, with no notification type page. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-006)

The home's 'Live animals' section has a 'View dashboard' link and two glance cards, 'Action needed' ('Tasks requiring your attention', a count, 'View tasks') and 'Status updates' ('Changes in the past 24 hours', a count, 'View updates'), counted from the organisation's notifications. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-008, p13-009, p13-013)

The Live animals page has the caption 'Dashboard', the heading 'Live animals', a Back link to the home, 'Create new' and 'Use template' buttons, a 'Summary' of the two glance cards counted for live animals, and a 'Notifications' section holding the list. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-015, p13-019, p13-021, p13-022, p13-024, p13-025; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p1-043; prototype:dr2-1-specs p5-037)

The Status updates count is 0 and its 'Changes in past 24 hours' page is built and empty; there are no Delayed states, no inspection card or page and no Messages link. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-087, p13-088, p13-090; repo:insbackend p1-022)
The home shows no section for any notification type other than live animals. (prototype:dr2-1-source p13-010)

dashboard and address book live in the INS frontend

openQuestions: c-005: Does any notification type other than live animals come into this programme? Default followed: no; 'Create new' starts the live-animals journey with no type page, and the home shows only the Live animals section.
c-004: Where do the live-animals journey's dashboard links go? Default followed: to the INS dashboard; the animals frontend's own dashboard stays unchanged until a ruling retires it.

c-006: What is built for states no real service records? Default followed: the Status updates card and its changes page are built but stay empty (count 0); Delayed, inspection and Messages are not built.
increments.notes: Combines the home, the Live animals page and the empty states: one page structure around the list inc-035 to inc-039 build. Depends on inc-039 (the Action needed count and page), inc-017 (Manage templates, which 'Use template' opens) and inc-016 (the animals frontend's Dashboard item goes to the INS dashboard).
